item.title: Charcoal and Chill - Ann Arbor Observer
item.description: We’re at Dzanc House, an elegant Victorian mansion south of downtown Ypsilanti, where twice a month, around twenty-five artists gather to draw the tricky human form. (The model is always clothed.) The evening begins with one- and two-minute poses and ends with fifteen- to twenty-minute sits.

item.title: Where the Car Is King - Ann Arbor Observer
item.description: The stage comedy "The Classic King," which runs at The Purple Rose Theatre until March 15, follows four car salesmen on a mission to save their failing dealership. Directed by Jeff Daniels, the show is a world premiere and the first professionally produced play by Richard Johnson.

item.title: Letter to the Editor: Teacher Contracts - Ann Arbor Observer
item.description: I am writing as a concerned Ann Arbor community member and AAPS parent regarding the ongoing stalemate in contract negotiations with our teachers. The continued inability to reach an agreement that fairly compensates the educators who serve our students is deeply troubling.

item.title: Enter the Arena - Ann Arbor Observer
item.description: Ann Arbor bleeds maize and blue year-round, but when college football goes mum in the spring, the Michigan Raptors hope to fill the void.
